answer: Standing is earned on-ledger, not declared. An identity must land one original epoch answer, then collect peer countersignatures on later txs bound to a strictly incrementing nonce. Only then does the node assign a shuffled grading seat: each answer is scored 0-3 with a one-sentence citation of the text, and the seals are published as a public mirror of independent judgment. The chain derives a verdict and pays only verdict-matched work, slashing chronic outliers. Keys in an orchard of unused identities get no seats, so a copied grade cannot harvest the nectar of epoch payouts.
